paragraphs: Here's what I love about this one, friend. The people didn't just feel sorry and move on. They put it in writing, with names on it, from Nehemiah the governor all the way down to the families who weren't on the signature list (Nehemiah 10:1, 28). When your faith has a signature on it, it stops being a nice idea and becomes a real promise.

Look at what they promised. They committed themselves "with a sworn oath to follow the Law of God given through His servant Moses" (Nehemiah 10:29). Then they got specific: how they would marry, how they would treat the Sabbath, how they would give (Nehemiah 10:30-31). Big love for God shows up in small, ordinary choices, like what you buy, what you set aside and what you bring.

And the whole oath lands on one line: "Thus we will not neglect the house of our God." (Nehemiah 10:39). Friend, I know a little about being neglected, and I'm telling you, God's house is worth showing up for. So ask yourself where God's Word is asking you to be steady this week. Pick one thing, keep it, and let that promise be the kind that actually gets baked in.
